title: Hybrid cache offload follows consumer synchronization, not inheritance symmetry
applies_when: A cache combines KV attention with convolution or recurrent states and a proposed offload/prefetch repair calls every parent method, especially dynamic/static sliding-window subclasses.
lesson: Trace each state's consumer and its stream-wait protocol separately. A KV prefetch wait does not make a linear-state consumer offload-aware. In the cited hybrid cache fix, only KV moves to CPU and back; conv/recurrent states stay on GPU. Explicitly dispatch the KV parent for sliding classes and exclude all hybrid variants from linear-only cache classification. Check actual state devices and unchanged values across a real offload/prefetch round trip, with matched parent/fix sources and full/sliding, dynamic/static coverage. Similar method names or symmetric parent calls are not sufficient evidence.
avoid_when: A different cache may synchronize every consumer or intentionally support linear-state offload. This does not prohibit that design. The tiny synchronized round-trip check does not prove asynchronous race freedom, model generation correctness, transfer overlap, throughput, or all cache implementations. An existing author's closed PR is still prior work; coordinate rather than claiming its repair as a new discovery.

evidence.note: Author-owned GH-48947 fix changes KV dispatch/resident linear states and classification for four hybrid cache classes. Independent tiny real-CUDA check on the direct parent fails all four class contracts; this fix passes all four with exact KV/linear values. This is component evidence, not model, timing or upstream acceptance.
The repair is prior work in a larger PR. Its other changes and publication status are not qualified by the independent cache check.
